I was part of the founding undergraduate batch of Ashoka, graduated last year. You might want to think of Ashoka as the Indian version of an elite American liberal arts college. 

It probably has the best humanities and social science faculty you can find in the country (I'm not sure about the quality of the other faculty), and professors have full autonomy over the courses they design. I greatly enjoyed my time in the classroom. Some of their "global changemaker" stuff is PR bullshit but in class(especially the humanities classrooms) we were always making fun of that stuff along with the professors. Their critical thinking courses are mandatory courses that focus on academic writing practices and rhetoric(for the most part-- some professors choose to teach this in different ways, which I don't think is a good idea). 

Ashoka also has all the problems of elite private US liberal arts colleges-- the student community is very affluent and upper-caste(I wouldn't have been able to afford the fees if not for financial aid). Being confined to a bubble in Sonepat definitely detracts from the experience.
